To the right of the old woman, a tall man in a tuxedo adjusts his bowtie in a cracked mirror. Behind him, a girl in a tutu ties her ballet slippers, leaning against a stack of scenery flats. A stagehand in a black shirt hands a roll of duct tape to the girl in the tutu. Above them, a ladder leans against the wall, with a painter in white coveralls standing on the third rung, holding a brush. The painter looks down at a bucket of blue paint placed on the floor below. A parrot in a cage hangs from the ceiling above the costume rack, squawking at a mouse scurrying along the baseboard. The mouse hides behind a heavy velvet curtain that is partially drawn back. A security guard in a uniform stands by the exit door, checking his watch. He looks toward a technician in a headset who is crouching near a soundboard. The technician plugs a cable into the board while glancing at the security guard. There is no sunlight streaming through windows. There is no digital equipment visible.
